description:
Found by the specled_-dn4.9 audit (2026-07-26T00:25:30Z) while tracing item 2's path-identity fold. This is a real defect, not a cleanup.

dn4.5 normalized the per-test lane to repo-relative path identity, and dn4.9 item 2 extended repo-relative :files into the v1 records. But the v1 file-level detectors still join those repo-relative :files / owned_files against ABSOLUTE closure_files derived from raw module_info(:compile)[:source] — see lib/mix/tasks/spec.triangle.ex:447 and lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:132. A repo-relative string can never equal an absolute one, so execution_reach and untested_realization can never match.

Impact: those two detectors silently report nothing rather than reporting wrongly — same silent-failure class this epic spent the day correcting on the per-test lane, now visible on the v1 lane.

Fix: extend dn4.5's per_test_path_identity normalization to the v1 path so both sides of the join agree. Verify by constructing a case that SHOULD match and asserting it does — the current tests pass because nothing ever matches.

comments.text: Base decision: the defect only exists on the dn4 epic branch (specled_-dn4/fast-follow-per-test) — main's Formatter.source_file/1 still stores absolute paths, so the v1 join works on main. dn4.9 item 2's repo_relative_path in formatter.ex is what broke the join, and the fix must extend repo_relative_source_path (dn4.5 lane), which doesn't exist on main. Staging from epic HEAD ddda892; fix ships with the epic, never reaching main broken.

Notes (advisory — none of these change the verdict):
1. `binding_present?` semantics quietly widened. Both producers derive `binding_present?: closure_files != []` (coverage_closure.ex:123, spec.triangle.ex:432). Because `mfa_source_file/1` now returns `[]` for an out-of-repo source instead of an absolute path, a requirement whose closure resolves *entirely* to out-of-repo modules now reports `binding_present?: false` — "this requirement has no realization" — which suppresses `branch_guard_untested_realization` on both the v1 lane (coverage_triangulation.ex:579) and the aggregate v2 lane (coverage_triangulation.ex:986). Pre-fix those closures were absolute-but-present and the finding fired. This is the "fail toward silence" direction that `specled.decision.coverage_identity_joins` — an ADR this very subject lists — was written to prevent ("unresolved compile sources" are supposed to land in an explicit unknown partition, which the v1 lane has none of). I am *not* calling this a Gap because it is unreachable in normal use: the compile tracer records every remote callee unfiltered (compiler/tracer.ex:164-173), so real closures mix repo and stdlib/dep MFAs and always retain at least the effective binding's own repo file; an all-out-of-repo closure needs either a subject bound solely to a dep module or a build whose compile-time directory differs from `File.cwd!()` (shared `_build` across worktrees, CI artifact restore). `_build` is worktree-local here, so neither holds today. Suggest a follow-up ticket to give the v1 lane an explicit unresolved-source partition rather than folding it into `binding_present?`.
2. Four copies of the same helper now exist: `Coverage.Formatter.repo_relative_path/1` (formatter.ex:277), `CoverageTriangulation.repo_relative_source_path/1` (:452), and the two added by this ticket. They are byte-identical logic and must stay in lockstep for the join to hold; nothing enforces that. A shared `SpecLedEx.Coverage.Paths` would make the ADR's "one stable path identity" structural instead of conventional.
3. Spec wording lags the code. `specled.triangulation.per_test_path_identity` scopes its mandate to "the per-test line→MFA join", so it does not literally cover the v1 *file-level* join this ticket fixed. The fix is still correct — untested_realization and execution_reach_metric implicitly require a workable join — but no requirement states the v1 file-level identity contract outright, which is why the defect could exist without failing a spec gate. Worth a wording extension when that subject is next edited.
